examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Variance Given the Number, Sum, and Sum of Squares of the Data Points
examples.problem:
Compute the variance $\sigma^2$ of a data set $x_i$ consisting of $8$ data points, where

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i = 40, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i^2 = 320.
$$
examples.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
\sigma^2 = \overline{x^2} - (\overline{x})^2,
$$

where $\overline{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overline{x^2}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overline{x}.$ There are $n=8$ points in our data set, and we know that $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i = 40,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 40 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ We know that $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i^2 = 320,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 320 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =40-{(5)}^{2} \\  & =40-25 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
14,\,21,\,13,\,16
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ is the mean of the data set.

First, we need to compute the mean. There are $n=4$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (14+21+13+16) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 64 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(14-16)^{2}+(21-16)^{2}+(13-16)^{2}+(16-16)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[4+25+9+0] \\  & =\frac{38}{4} \\  & =9.5.\end{aligned}
$$
